answer: Separate batch and speed paths (Lambda): batch recomputes every result from full history on a schedule, speed covers only events since the last batch run, and the serving layer merges them at the batch boundary hour. Correctness comes from the batch overwrite, but each layer holds its own copy of the logic, so the two drift and the boundary hour can disagree. Reprocessing means rerunning the batch job. One job definition (Kappa or bounded/unbounded) keeps 1 code path and 1 output table with no merge. Correctness comes from handling late data in the stream, and reprocessing is a replay of the retained log through the same job. This needs enough log retention and good late-event handling.
